This High-End Papago Vans Transit Proves Rugged and Cozy Can Coexist in a Camper Van
25 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans
Naturally, the limited interior space in a camper van makes it impossible for you to fit all the comforts you have in a conventional home (unless you're living in a really small apartment). That said, a clever camper van design should be able to pack most luxuries people need – that's the case with the rig I'm checking out today.
What we have here is a conversion based on an AWD Ford Transit with an extended 148" wheelbase. It was created by Papago Vans, a Mesa, Arizona-based company specializing in transforming vans into adventure machines.
The vehicle's exterior is pretty indicative toward its "camper DNA" due to the various upgrades . First off, the van rides on Black Rhino wheels wrapped in all-terrain tires.
At the front, Papago Vans installed a CATuned bumper complete with two D-Ring recovery points and a hitch receiver. A CAtuned skidplate underneath, as well as a differential skid plate offer extra protection for the engine base. On the opposite end, you'll come across a spare tire carrier / ladder combo.
It's clear that the customer wants to take this van off the beaten path. Besides a suitable wheel and tire combo, they opted for a Van Compass Stage 3 Topo 2.0 suspension kit, which comes with Falcon rear shocks, a front lift kit, a rear mini leaf spring pack, and high clearance rear shock brackets.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans Climbing on top of the vehicle was made easy thanks to an FVC (Flatline Van Co.) ladder permanently fixed on the driver's side. It leads to an FVC Safari roof rack holding two 200 W solar panels, an awning, and light pods on the sides; the customer will also fit a StarLink Mini antenna. The roof also has a Maxxair Deluxe vent fan and a Nomadic Cooling Co. A/C unit.
Other notable mods include Steelcraft side steps, CR Laurence half-slider windows, power and water connections, and flares. Flares, also known as pods or capsules, are designed to increase the van width to allow builders to fit beds in east to west arrangements instead of the standard north to south.
This rig's flares are finished in matte black, matching the rest of the exterior mods, and come with half-slider windows.
The interior has an open layout, meaning there's no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. Thanks to the driver and passenger seat swivel bases, you can turn them around to face the back of the van.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for soft blue laminated cabinetry, white shiplap walls, a stained wood ceiling, and wood-imitating LVP (luxury vinyl plank) flooring. The look is complemented by a bamboo countertop and various black accents, such as the kitchen hardware or the cabinet and drawer handles.
Dead ahead of the entrance, Papago Vans devised a two-person Alpine bench complete with a Lagun table mount. It's also mounted on a swivel base, so it can be turned to face either the entrance or the cabin. The practical thing about it is that it can be folded flat into a tiny bed.
A cabinet above the bench hides the rig's "command center." It includes a touchscreen display that allows you to monitor and control the power system, as well as switches for a water heater, Wi-Fi router, shower drain, water pump, and a freeze protection system.
Next, we have the kitchen, which is split into two units. It features a deep stainless steel sink with a cutting board cover and a filtered water faucet, a 700 W microwave oven, and an Isotherm fridge with a tiny freezer compartment.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans You'll have to use a portable stove for cooking. What's more, a Maxxair vent fan is perfectly positioned above to draw out the smells and fumes from cooking.
Two overhead cabinets, three drawers, and a cabinet underneath the sink are available for storage in the kitchen unit on the passenger side. The latter houses a Guzzle H2O water filtration system.
On the opposite side, a floor-to-ceiling storage unit integrates an overhead cabinet, a closet with hanging space, and four drawers.
Finally, the bedroom takes up the rear part of the living space. Comfort is ensured by a queen-size bed with a memory foam mattress, arranged side to side thanks to the flares I mentioned earlier.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans The bedroom also offers two reading lights, two overhead cabinets, charging points, a 32-inch TV attached to a wall swivel mount, and a Sirocco swivel fan. Moreover, a ceiling A/C unit can quickly cool the entire interior.
Like in most vans with fixed bed arrangements, the space underneath the bed was turned into a garage, accessible from both inside and outside the van. Besides offering a bunch of room for storage, it accommodates the utility systems in boxes on its sides.
Power is on the left side – the electrical system's highlights are a 920 Ah Epoch lithium battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter/charger.
Thanks to three charging sources, running out of battery will be a challenge, at least if you drive consistently and/or you keep the van in a sunny environment. You can use shore power, solar power , and DC-DC charging while the engine is running.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 33-gallon (125-liter) freshwater tank, an under-mounted greywater tank with a heating pad and an electronic ball valve, a water heater, and an outdoor shower connection. Furthermore, an Espar heater that's tapped into the vehicle's fuel tank can make the interior nice and toasty when needed.
As you've already seen, there's no fixed bathroom inside the van. However, you can shower inside the van thanks to a Tetravan shower installed by the entrance. This space-saving solution has a folding aluminum pan and a water mixer that can be easily set up and used. To complete the shower, you must also attach a curtain to the ceiling.
All in all, Papago Vans has the ideal combo between rugged adventure capabilities and a cozy, well-equipped living space. If you want to adventure off-road and stay off-grid for a while, this is the perfect van to do it in.

Ben Affleck Goes Behind the Camera for Ford's F-150 Raptor Story, Casts Real Engineers
32 photos
Photo: Ford From the Road
Ford Racing has just launched a high-profile ad campaign to mark the 16-year story and raw origin of the Ford F-150 Raptor. Titled "Project Raptor: Based on a Ford Story," the short film is directed by Oscar winner and Raptor owner Ben Affleck and stars fellow actor and Raptor owner (no surprise there!) Jon Bernthal.
Bernthal is actually the narrator alongside the actual engineering masterminds who secretly brought the mighty truck to life. Now, they reveal how the first-ever Ford F-150 Raptor came to life. Back in 2006, a small group of Ford Racing engineers pivoted from street performance to ask a wild question: Could the high-speed capability of a Baja 1000 desert race truck be brought directly to a production vehicle?
They already had the answer to that. They knew they could do it. However, they had to face massive internal skepticism. Traditional 4x4s focused on low-range crawling, not flying over sand dunes at high speeds. The project was canceled not once, not twice, but six separate times before it finally got the green light.
The "Raptor" designation was entirely accidental. It was never intended to be the final production name for the super truck. It started as an internal development codename, but it grew on those involved, and it generated so much excitement that Ford fought for the naming rights.
Photo: Ford From the Road When Ford first decided to use it for the production model, they discovered that Mosler Automotive, a boutique American supercar manufacturer, already legally owned the trademark rights to the “Raptor” name. Ford could not legally sell a vehicle under that badge until their legal team negotiated an undisclosed financial settlement with Mosler to purchase the naming rights.
Furthermore, when Ford tried to expand its truck lineup globally with the Ranger Raptor, they hit a massive roadblock in Australia. Hino Motors, the commercial truck division of Toyota, had owned the Australian trademark for the designation since the early 1990s.
And the fight was far from over. Ford's legal battles for the name did not stop with real cars. They also had to fight over toy cars. When the Jurassic World movie franchise took off, Universal Studios filed a trademark for the term "Raptor Squad" to launch a line of toy cars based on the velociraptors in the movie.
Ford opposed Universal in court, arguing that a line of dinosaur-themed toy trucks called "Raptor Squad" would directly dilute Ford’s merchandise, confusing buyers who associated the name with the F-150 pickup truck . Universal ultimately agreed to amend their trademark description so it wouldn't conflict with real or toy automotive goods.
Photo: Ford From the Road Instead of actors, Ben Affleck chose real engineers for his 90-second fillm. The newly launched commercial puts the spotlight on the Ford Racing engineers who withstood the long sleepless nights and brutal desert testing to roll out a truck that would perform both on and off the road.
Derek Bier, the Chief Engineer of Ford Racing, literally spent so much time testing the truck in Mexico that he learned Spanish. In the meantime, the Vehicle Architecture and CAE Manager, Tim Smith, was the one who built the truck’s tough skeletal structure. Then, there is Chris Paiva, Vehicle Dynamics Manager, affectionately called "The Raptor Guy." He helped integrate the iconic long-travel FOX Live Valve suspension technology.
What started as a low-profile engineering experiment has grown into a massively popular model and the beginning of a new segment. Sixteen years later, Ford hosted a massive Raptor Rally in Lake Havasu, Arizona, drawing over 1,100 people and 500 Raptor trucks to trail ride and share their experience.

BMW TX5 M60 Sport Truck Rendering Proposes a Neue Klasse Spartanburg Version of the Ford F-150 Icon
10 photos
Photo: jlord8 / Instagram
The G65 iteration of the BMW X5 mid-size luxury crossover SUV was introduced for the 2027 model year for all the main markets (Europe, North America, China) with a few premieres, but that’s seemingly not enough for some folks, including the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI.
Succeeding the G05 iteration launched in production in 2018, the fifth iteration is almost completely different from its predecessors except for the continued use of the Cluster Architecture (CLAR) platform. But it now comes with an enhanced version that allows the use of no fewer than five powertrain options: gasoline, diesel, plug-in hybrid, as well as battery or fuel cell electric versions.
Aside from that, it’s completely new, featuring the Neue Klasse styling inside and outside. One thing that stays the same is the production location in the United States at BMW Plant Spartanburg in South Carolina. Currently, BMW only offers the 2027 X5 40 xDrive in the United States, kicking off at $72,100 sans destination, sporting the company’s 3.0-liter BMW M TwinPower Turbo inline 6-cylinder with xDrive all-wheel drive, rocking 394 hp and a 28 MPG rating plus a sprint to 60 mph in 5.1 seconds.
More versions are set to follow, including the pure V8-powered BMW X5 M60 xDrive that represents the North American counterpart of the European X5 M60e xDrive high-performance PHEV, but with an enhanced version of BMW’s S68 twin-turbo 4.4-liter V8 churning out in excess of 600 hp and 590 lb-ft of torque.
Production will start next spring in America, according to the rumor mill, and the V8 model could arrive at US dealerships as a late 2027 model year or even as a 2028MY with an estimated starting MSRP of around $95k. That’s cool, right? But what if the BMW X5 M60 xDrive also arrived with a new body style, too?
Well, that’s probably not going to happen in the real world, but only across Imagination Land thanks to Jim, a virtual artist known as " jlord8 " on social media who loves messing around with all things CGI from the automotive realm, and now he dreams of a wacky BMW.
More precisely, his latest unofficial, hypothetical design project doesn’t focus on a new Mazda or any of the American brands. Instead, he envisions the possibility of a BMW TX5 M60 luxury Single Cab sport truck for our consideration, aiming for something different across the full-size truck segment. Of course, he had to have a starting point, and the Ford F-150 served as the initial template before applying the G65’s Neue Klasse design, especially at the front.
So, what do you think – yay or nay? Would you buy something like this? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Jim (@jlord8)

CHINA - 2024/06/21: In this photo illustration, the American publicly traded aerospace and defense corporation General Dynamics Corporation (GD, NYSE: GD) logo seen displayed on a smartphone with an economic stock exchange index graph in the background. (Photo Illustration by Budrul Chukrut/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)
WASHINGTON — General Dynamics Information Technology (GDIT) has a new leader, with company veteran Amy Johnson announced today as incoming president.
Johnson replaces longtime president Amy Gilliland, who was let go from the company earlier this month after almost a decade of leading the business unit. Paul Nedzbala has been serving as acting president in the interim.
“Amy has a proven track record of leading teams to solve complex and highly technical challenges for our customers,” said Phebe Novakovic, the outgoing CEO of General Dynamics , in the announcement. “I am confident that her dynamic leadership, operational rigor and deep commitment to our values and culture will deliver value to our customers, employees and shareholders.”
According to the press release, Johnson is a 27-year veteran of General Dynamics Mission Systems. She was most recently vice president and general manager for Space, Cyber and Intelligence, and has background experience “across cybersecurity, defense electronics, space and intelligence systems.”
Johnson will begin her role as president on Nov. 3.
One of the biggest players in federal IT, GDIT provides critical cyber, software and networking tools to both the military and civilian sector agencies ranging from enterprise to tactical edge applications. The capabilities enable secure communications, full-spectrum cyber operations and monitoring of threats to networks.

1961 Chrysler Newport Wagon Has Massive V8 Under the Hood To Prove Old-School Is Still Cool
38 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
This 1961 Chrysler Newport Wagon came to life as an entry-level premium family hauler, but it left stock days far behind. The wagon has undergone a heart transplant, transforming it into a hot power wagon that proves that old-school is still cool, no matter the body style.
Back in 1961, the Newport was reintroduced as Chrysler’s low-priced full-size model lineup. It dropped as a major success. Undercutting the flagship New Yorker by nearly $2,000, the Newport helped the brand financially with its base models. 1961 also marked the final year for Chrysler’s large rear tailfins, which this car proudly retains
This build, however, spins around the engine bay. That is where the magic hides. Out went the original factory 361-cubic-inch Firebolt V8 with 265 horsepower, and in went the TNT-style 440-cubic-inch (7.2-liter) Mopar big-block V8 engine for an explosive kind of road behavior.
However, the listing fails to disclose how much the massive power plant makes under the hood of the Chrysler Newport Wagon right now. Depending on the exact donor year and configuration, a vintage Mopar 440 big-block with a four-barrel carburetor traditionally produced between 350 and 375 gross horsepower from the factory.
Photo: Bring a Trailer With only minor modern upgrades, like aftermarket ignition or intake components, a big-block 440-cubic-inch V8 easily pushes 400 to 500 horsepower. The listing does mention a minor issue where the engine bogs slightly under hard acceleration at times, signaling that the fuel or the ignition timing might require some fine-tuning by its next owner.
What we do know is that an aftermarket oil pressure gauge was mounted directly to the engine firewall. The monstrous power plant throws power to the ground through the rear wheels with the help of a period-correct TorqueFlite three-speed automatic transmission. The driver operates it via the push-button gear selector, built right into the left side of the dashboard panel.
The 1961 Chrysler Newport mirrors Virgil Exner's vision The 1961 Chrysler Newport represents the ultimate peak of Chrysler's space-age Forward Look design era, orchestrated by design guru Virgil Exner. The boldly-styled model that you are looking at is a rare Town & Country hardtop wagon.
This means that it features a continuous open cabin layout with no fixed B-pillar between the front and rear doors. When all side windows are down, the layout creates a sleek, uninterrupted silhouette. When the doors open, those getting on board have unrestricted access.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Up front, the Newport features the iconic angled quad headlights , flanking an aggressively styled, inverse-trapezoidal grille. The striking two-tone Teal Blue and White paint frames the radical, razor-sharp finned rear quarter panels. The wagon rolls on 15-inch chrome wire wheels wrapped in General Ameritrac SE white-stripe tires.
The cabin looks like an incredibly detailed mix of vintage 1960s design and modern luxury. Full-width benches are covered in custom plush parchment leather with pleated inserts. The driver sits in front of Chrysler’s three-dimensional AstraDome control pod.
The futuristic, standalone dome houses a sweep speedometer scaled up to 120 mph (193 kph), sitting alongside gauges that track the fuel level, amperage, coolant temperature, and oil pressure. A remote mirror control and an analog clock are also on board. The car is equipped with air conditioning. The belts, compressor, and pulleys are intact, but the lines and under-dash unit have gone missing.
No garage queen here The five-digit odometer reads nearly 97,000 miles, which means it hasn't spent its entire life locked away in a garage. The one trying to sell the Chrysler Newport Wagon has only driven it 50 miles before he parked it indefinitely. That explains why he is trying to get rid of it now. However, he might have started on the wrong foot by setting a reserve that is too high.
Photo: Bring a Trailer The trunk hosts a stowable, rear-facing third-row bench seat that folds entirely flat into the floor to open up a massive cargo space. To get into those seats, you roll down the power-operated rear window and lower the bottom tailgate.
Instead of the all-drum setup, upgraded power-assisted disc brakes up front and the traditional drums out back provide the stopping power. The car rolled off the production line with power steering back in 1961.
Fast forward to 2026, and the 1961 Chrysler Newport Wagon was auctioned off on Bring a Trailer, but bidding stopped at $28,250, which was under the undisclosed reserve. So the owner is currently stuck with the wagon. The car has been under his ownership for the past five years. He bought it on the same platform back in 2021, after it had reportedly spent 25 years with one family.
It was that family that changed its original white paint to the teal blue and white combination during restoration. Offered with a clean Washington title, it does, however, have some flaws after so many years on the road. The listing notes touch-up paint on the passenger quarter panel, rust repair on the tailgate, and lifting paint on the grille.
Well, maybe the owner will get better luck next time...

Toyota Tundra Goes Single Cab; It's a Short-Bed Sport Truck Now, Though Only Across Imagination Land
8 photos
Photo: abimelecdesign / Instagram
When Toyota Motor North America reported its September and third-quarter 2026 sales results, the highlights were on the electrified models and the namesake Toyota brand.
TMNA sold 201,306 vehicles, up 8.4 percent, in September 2026 across the US automotive market, and for the third quarter it reported deliveries of 633,223 vehicles, up 0.6 percent. The namesake Toyota division sold 171,469 vehicles during the past month, up 7.9 percent, while the quarter was finished with over 540k deliveries, up only 0.5%.
Year-to-date, TMNA reached 1,876,614 units, up 0.6%, while Toyota was up by 1.2% to almost 1.614 million vehicles, as Lexus dragged them down via its three-percent negative performance to less than 263k units. Anyway, Toyota can’t fully bank on the all-new RAV4 for its return to higher positive results because it’s still ramping up.
Instead, it got a helping hand from the Corolla, Camry, bZ, Corolla Cross, Grand Highlander, 4Runner, Sequoia, Sienna, and Tacoma nameplates. Not the bigger Tundra, though, which is slightly down by almost one percentage point. Well, the XK70 third generation is actually holding up pretty well given that it’s been around since the 2022 model year and so far, Toyota hasn’t issued a mid-cycle refresh procedure, only model year enhancements.
While we’re patiently waiting for the facelift, someone had an idea – a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI. More precisely, Abimelec Arellano, a virtual artist better known as " abimelecdesign " on social media, has prepared the newest wishful-thinking project - a cool Tundra truck.
His unofficial, hypothetical design project centers around the option of a Toyota Tundra Single Cab model with a short bed – aka a sport truck like in the good old days. To make it happen, he crafted a modified hood, lengthened the doors a little bit, along with the “bed in order to get those single cab proportions just right.” He also added “a ground effects kit and custom wheels,” and mixed a spectacular orange hue with black trim elements and a bedliner.
Last but not least, he asks us about the engine to be used with this potentially sporty model. Well, quite obviously, if the pixel master wanted our five cents on the matter, it would absolutely need the upcoming hybrid V8 used by the Gazoo Racing GR GT supercar. That way it could fight the 2027 Ram 1500 Rumble Bee SRT without breaking a sweat.
If that’s not possible even across Imagination Land, we’d think it suffices with the current 3.4 L V35A-FTS twin-turbo V6 rocking 437 hp. That way it might still compete with the entry-level tiers of the Rumble Bee and also with the Ford F-150 Lobo. What do you think – yay or nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Abimelec Arellano (@abimelecdesign)

GM Is Shutting Down Its Battery Plant in Detroit
10 photos
Photo: General Motors
General Motors is shutting down its Brownstown Battery Assembly plant in Detroit, Michigan. The auto giant is planning to wind down operations at the 480,000-square-foot facility by next summer, when its current lease expires.
The Brownstown facility, which opened back in 2009, was primarily dedicated to low-volume, niche electrified components. The facility assembled high-voltage battery packs for GM’s ultra-luxury flagship EV, the Cadillac Celestiq. It also produced both the electric motors and battery packs for the first-ever hybrid Corvette and housed a short-lived joint venture with Honda to develop hydrogen fuel cell technology.
The shutdown stems from shifting vehicle production lifecycles, dissolving partnerships, and EV market meltdown. In production for nearly three years at the GM Bowling Green Assembly Plant in Kentucky, the Corvette E-Ray has been phased out after a short-lived glory and replaced by the Corvette Grand Sport X.
In the meantime, the Celestiq , which sees the light of day at the auto group’s tech center in Warren, Michigan, remains an exclusive, low-run flagship product.. Only 25 units of the Cadillac Celestiq were produced for its initial 2025 model year, with total lifetime deliveries across both the 2025 and 2026 model years estimated to still be well under 100 units.
Furthermore, the hydrogen partnership with Honda is dissolving, bringing nearly a decade of formal collaboration to a close. Operating under the name Fuel Cell System Manufacturing LLC (FCSM) and taking up roughly 80,000 square feet of the Brownstown plant, the two automakers agreed to completely discontinue the fuel cell system project at their Michigan facility.
Due to progressive production cuts, staffing at the plant had already been reduced from a peak of 300 down to fewer than a dozen employees. Under General Motors' agreement with the UAW union, these remaining workers are being offered transfers to other nearby facilities. They were notified about the change earlier this year.
The lease expiration officially brings operations at one of GM's earliest electrification sites to a close as GM is adjusting its original aggressive EV strategy in response to softer-than-expected consumer demand and changing federal regulations, which prompted a shift back to gas-powered trucks and high-margin models.
The ongoing assembly and component production handled by the Brownstown site will be transferred to other active General Motors facilities across the country, Automotive News reports. In the meantime, the auto giant has incurred a total of $11.2 billion in EV-related charges for scaling back its electric vehicle footprint and addressing supplier settlements.
A person familiar with the matter confirmed for Automotive News that the plant will be decommissioned by next summer, when the lease comes to an end. The decision comes after GM announced it would pull the plug on the $2.5 billion battery plant in Lansing, now exclusively operated by LG Energy Solution.
As a backup plan, General Motors took over the long-term lease of the building, originally planned to be used for its subsequently canceled Piston Automotive partnership, but has yet to decide what it will do with it.

Owner of 30 Years Lets Go of His Dream Car 1970 Hemi Cuda 4-Speed To Take Care of His Wife
65 photos
Photo: YouTube/Mopars5150
The golden era of American muscle cars produced few machines as universally revered or fiercely contested on the auction block as the Plymouth Hemi Cuda. While pristine, untouched factory survivors often dominate the headlines, the cars that lived through decades of devoted enthusiast ownership carry an equally captivating gravitas. This red gem has had only two owners in 56 years.
Some people never learn how many cars is too many cars, because there’s always that one Hemi Mopar that’s just too good to leave behind, because it might just turn out to be “the one that got away,” in a hypothetical future where the car nut simply walks away from Providence’s offering.
Days before acquiring a black 1971 Plymouth Cuda 440 Six-Barrel 4-speed at the Barrett-Jackson auction in Las Vegas (for $363,000), Troy Bergeron of Mopars5150 had his son Davis steer a flatbed hauler across the Mojave Desert toward southern Arizona. The destination was a private garage in Hereford, just south of Tucson near the Mexican border. Waiting beneath a protective plastic sheet was a striking Rallye Red 1970 Plymouth Hemi Cuda that had remained with the same caretaker for 30 years.
That might just as well have been 30 minutes, when it comes to Hemicudas, there are very little details that can take precedence over those two four-letter words (Hemi and Cuda), which some marketing genius over at Plymouth decided to say in one breath, and spell it accordingly on the shaker hood scoop.
Photo: YouTube/Mopars5150 The long-term owner, a 74-year-old lifelong Mopar devotee named Jim, greeted Davis Bergeron standing in front of his two E-bodies, and pulled back the cover to reveal his prized possession. Growing up as a dedicated street racer in Lowell, Massachusetts, and spending decades around New England Dragway and Maine car shows, Jim always viewed the 1970 Hemi Cuda as the ultimate muscle car. Three decades ago, he finally fulfilled that lifelong dream by purchasing the coupe.
(Fine, the E-bodies weren’t muscle cars, but pony cars, as the title rightfully belonged to the B-body band – Road Runner, GTX, Superbird, Charger, Coronet, Daytona – but tell me if a 426 Hemi anything can be considered “muscle” or not).
Jim acquired the car in 1996 directly from its original owner, a Florida collector who reportedly housed 250 Hemi vehicles at the time (I have a challenge for you, waiting at the end of the story, regarding this particular provenance detail). When the current owner took delivery, the odometer displayed a little over 32,000 miles, though the vehicle was essentially a basket case wearing faded original paint and lacking both its factory engine and transmission.
Photo: YouTube/Mopars5150 Undeterred, Jim commissioned a comprehensive rotisserie restoration, investing $100,000 into the build during the mid-1990s. That’s how you make a small fortune while supporting this hobby: you start out with a big fortune.
Because original 426-cubic-inch Hemi blocks frequently suffered from cracking through the main webs, Jim opted for a brand-new Mopar high-performance crate block with high nickel content. Renowned engine builder Larry Shepard assembled the powerhouse, boring and stroking the displacement to 472 cubes while retaining the correct 1970 cylinder heads, intake manifold, the two fours (that’s dual four-barrel carburetors, in case it’s not clear), and shaker hood assembly.
The motor was recently refreshed and carries just 10 break-in miles. Backing the 472-cubic-inch powerplant is a period-correct, non-numbers-matching 18-spline A833 4-speed manual transmission built by transmission specialist Joe Liberty, featuring a Hurst Pistol Grip shifter paired with a Super Shifter body and shortened levers for crisp, short throws.
Photo: YouTube/Mopars5150 The drivetrain channels power through a chromoly driveshaft to a 4.10 Dana 60 rear axle equipped with a Strange Engineering pinion and snubber, staying true to its factory Super Track Pak specification.
While the underside and engine bay were restored to show-winning standards, Jim incorporated select upgrades for reliability and performance. The car breathes through 2-inch Hooker headers feeding a 3-inch TTI dual exhaust system with an H-pipe and 3-inch chrome tips. It rides on 15-inch Rallye wheels, widened to ten inches in the rear, wrapped in meaty drag radials, while stainless steel brake lines replaced the original setup.
Inside the cabin, the Hemi Cuda retains its factory-installed seats, door panels, tinted glass, and dash pad, while the Rallye instrument cluster with its 150-mph speedometer and 8,000-rpm tachometer was professionally refurbished. Though ordered from the factory as a radio-delete vehicle, an aftermarket Alpine head unit was discreetly fitted, alongside a manual hand choke and rear window louvers crafted by Gene Gregory after Mopar discontinued the original factory parts.
Photo: YouTube/Mopars5150 Documentation accompanying the car includes a 1996 Virginia title copy and a 1996 Chrysler Registry report by authority Galen Govier confirming its pedigree. Built at the Hamtramck, Michigan plant on December 12, 1969, this car is one of 284 Hemi Cuda hardtops with a 4-speed produced for the United States in 1970. Factory options included FE5 Rallye Red paint, front and rear elastomeric bumpers, power brakes, hood pins, and a six-way adjustable bucket seat.
Over his 30-year stewardship, Jim never raced the car, driving it only in 15-mile or 20-mile increments to local gatherings and claiming Best of Show honors at New England Dragway. Fueled exclusively with 110-octane Sunoco racing gasoline and showing 40,483 miles on the odometer, the coupe remained his favorite among more than 150 Mopars he owned. Only failing health and the need to care for his wife forced the sale.
The historic significance of the Hemi Cuda stems from its brief production run during the peak of the horsepower wars. Offered strictly during the 1970 and 1971 model years on the third-generation E-body platform, the model was available in two body styles: hardtop and convertible. Buyers could pair the 425-horsepower 426-cubic-inch Hemi V8 with either the heavy-duty 4-speed manual or the A727 TorqueFlite 3-speed automatic transmission. Only 780 did.
Photo: YouTube/Mopars5150 Scarcity defines the Hemi Cuda legacy, as high insurance rates tightened the market. In 1970, Plymouth produced 652 Hemi Cuda hardtops and 14 convertibles, totaling 666 units. For 1971, output plummeted to 107 hardtops and seven convertibles. When new, the Cuda hardtop carried a base price of $3,164, while ticking the E74 code for the 426 Hemi option added a hefty $871.45 to the window sticker.
It wasn’t a cheap Plymouth anymore, it was a money-printing machine for tire companies – there were few other ways to sell rubber more efficiently than to wrap it on the business end of the seven-liter big-block from Ma’ Mopar.
In the collector market, those humble original figures have multiplied on a cosmic scale. Modified or non-numbers-matching 1970 Hemi Cuda hardtops like Jim's Rallye Red example command low six figures. Documented, numbers-matching hardtop coupes trade between $600,000 and $1,500,000.
Photo: YouTube/Mopars5150 The ultra-rare Hemi Cuda convertibles sit atop the muscle car hierarchy, crossing the auction block for sums between $2,000,000 and $3,500,000 as the undisputed crown jewels of Detroit iron. Speaking of which, let’s get back to the challenge I mentioned earlier. Jim said he bought the car in Florida, from a seller who owned 250 Hemi Mopars.
Do you think it’s just poetic license, or was there a real car nut that massive who actually had 2.5% of all 426-Street Hemi cars ever built? Or it could be that Jim counts first-gen hemi cars into this roll call? What’s even more intriguing is the fact that the car’s original title was issued in Virginia. That’s not inconsistent to the Florida sale – the first owner might have registered the car in Virginia, and simply stored it in the Sunshine State.

New BMW M3 Gearing Up To Rival AMG's C 63 and Audi's RS 5 – Rendering
6 photos
Photo: Kolesa
It’s been one month since BMW pulled the wraps off the new-generation 3 Series . Well, it’s not entirely new, because it features familiar underpinnings, as it is based on an updated version of the old car’s platform.
We are talking about the CLAR, and it’s not the Linie Grosse, which is the foundation stone of the old 7 Series, the demised 8 Series, the previous X5, outgoing X6, current X7, and XM, but the Linie Klein. In its previous configuration, it was used by the old 3 Series, as well as the previous-gen 5 Series, 6 Series, old X3, X4, Z4, Toyota GR Supra, and other models. And this construction will also be used on the upcoming M3.
BMW’s premium compact sports sedan will obviously live on to see a new generation, albeit a Neue Klasse one inside and out. But of course you already know that, because we have encountered plenty of prototypes in the open, and some of these have been used as blank canvases by the pixel altering crowd to create realistic digital illustrations. Thus, not only do we know that the new BMW M3 is indeed in the making, but we also know what it will look like, for the most part, anyway.
After all, it is not tricky at all to imagine the new-gen BMW 3 Series with a more aggressive design and a few other modifications, with some styling cues inspired by the M Concept Neue Klasse that was unveiled at the beginning of the year. Thus, if you feel like these renderings, which were signed by Kolesa’s Nikita Chuyko and released online a few days ago, are somewhat familiar, that’s because they use the new 3er as a starting point, as well as some features virtually borrowed from the study mentioned above.
Photo: Kolesa The car in question features a new hood that has a vented design, as well as an entirely new bumper at the front with extra lights on the sides, and it is these that have been inspired by the BMW M Concept Neue Klasse. The central part of the bumper, namely the air intakes, are quite similar to those of the regular 3er, and so is the grille, for that matter, as well as the headlights, including the yellow DRLs, which are a thing on the current range-topping version of the new-gen BMW 3 Series family, the M350 xDrive.
At the rear, we can see that this imagined new-gen BMW M3 sports a bumper that was also inspired by the one of the show car. It also has a pair of fake vents in the middle, a diffuser less aggressive than that of the M350, and a much chunkier ducktail spoiler. The taillights, and trunk lid are the same, and, quite surprisingly, so are the quad exhaust tips, from what we can tell. The wheels, however, are new, and very M-like, for that matter, and the car features an orange paint finish, a black roof, and other black details on the outside.
The quoted outlet is not famously known for releasing CGIs of the cockpits of its rendered models, but it is not hard to imagine what the interior of the all-new BMW M3 will look like. That’s because it will have the same dashboard panel as other Neue Klasse models, including the regular 3 Series, the i3, iX3, facelifted 7 Series, and new X5. This also means the Panoramic iDrive display stretching from one pillar to the other on the base of the windshield, as well as the same infotainment system.
Photo: Kolesa Sure, the screens will likely feature dedicated load screens and submenus, but overall, they will be the same. The steering wheel, on the other hand, should be different and a lot sportier, and we also expect the car to feature bucket seats for the driver and front passenger, as well as dedicated upholstery and trim, some M colors here and there, and a few other bits and bobs that will further separate the cabin of the new M3 from the regular 3 Series.
A familiar straight-six engine will sit under the hood of the upcoming BMW M3 , with twin turbocharging, a 3.0-liter displacement, and likely mild-hybrid assistance. We do not yet know any details about its power and torque, but let’s not forget that this model’s biggest rivals in the class, the Audi RS 5 and the Mercedes-AMG C 63, offer north of 600 horsepower, so it is only natural to expect the Munich company’s sports sedan (and station wagon) to have a similar output.
Word on the street is that the all-new BMW M3 will debut in 2028, roughly one year after its battery-electric sibling , the mechanically unrelated M3 Electric (based on the Neue Klasse platform), and we wouldn’t be surprised if it ends up looking like this CGI-infused model. But do you dig the design ?

London's Batman Is Giving Away Free Gas, Coffee, and Hope
8 photos
Photo: Instagram/London's Batman
A hero's work is never done, and Batman can vouch for that. Now that he's not actively fighting crime and preventing villains from doing whatever they're thinking of doing to the good people of Gotham, he's showing up for the people of London.
Indeed, Batman has made an appearance in the last place you'd expect him to pop up, doing things you least expected him to. He's taking his hero duties to London, where he's on a mission to bring back some hope and save civilians one day – and one stunt – at a time.
This reads like a joke, and I'm perfectly aware of it. It's not: there is a Batman in London and he's keeping his identity a secret for the time being, though you can bet your last dollar that he's not Bruce Wayne.
He calls himself London's Batman , breaking cover on social media on September 22, when he posted a video of himself in front of London Eye, announcing that "the Batman is here and the Batman is here to stay." Since then, he's been regularly updating the world on his good deeds, posting videos on platforms like Instagram and TikTok and then seeing them go viral.
Photo: Instagram/London's Batman Whoever Batman is, he's gone viral. And he's about as beloved as the fictional Batman from the comic books, before his fall from grace.
With stunts like the one he's been pulling, no wonder. Arriving at a moment when inflation in the UK is at its highest point, which brings high gas prices and higher-than-ever costs of living, Batman is doing whatever he can to bring some relief to the people – along with some hope.
So far, he's paid for people's gas, he's bought them coffee and gave them cheap meals, he's filled potholes, and he's handed out handheld fans to people on the subway to cool off. Other, sillier stunts saw him help a couple cross the street and sell Freddo candy bars for just 5 pence, as a reminder of how cheap they once were.
Photo: Instagram/London's Batman It would be easy to write off London's Batman as a guy in a rather ridiculous suit (*seriously, how heavy is that thing?!), pranking people for clicks. But at the end of the day, assuming none of the reactions are staged, he's really doing some good. He's also really bringing people some semblance of hope.
One of his most recent stunts was at a south-east London gas station, where he offered to pay for everyone's gas in a single day. The Daily Mail says that Batman actually offered £70 fuel vouchers to people who happened to drive by that day, with costs totaling about £3,500.
It's not like you could bring your entire group of friends, each in their own car, and fill the tank up completely. But it was still better than expected, a gas voucher offered as a gift. "We've been giving hundreds of people free fuel today in London," Batman said.
Photo: Instagram/London's Batman In another stunt, Batman went to Kingston Hospital, filming inside the crammed parking lot. It's always packed to the maximum, so people who drive themselves to the hospital always end up parking in areas nearby and, almost always, getting fined for it. People who need to go to the hospital shouldn't have to worry about parking fines, Batman decreed, heading to nearby streets and paying the fines of those who did get them.
Perhaps the best part is that each stunt is requested by the people. "Tell me your problems and Batman will make them go away" seems to be the Caped Crusader 's new motto, along with "We're trying to bring back hope to London."
Batman has help, not just the financial means to take requests for issues that need solving. When he was handing out handheld fans to commuters in late September, he was assisted by two sidekicks, both of them male, masked, and apparently British.
Photo: Instagram/London's Batman Before that, when Batman declared war to the garbage lining the streets of the British capital, he did so with help with from four mystery men.
He also has help from the community, like the restaurant owner who agreed to sell £1 chicken and chips for several days and the volunteers from the Youth Club who worked with him side by side filling potholes. Whether these people know his identity remains a mystery.
Speaking of the identity of this particular Batman, while we know for sure he's not Bruce Wayne, the Internet seems to believe he's Niko Omilana, a YouTube prankster, former contestant on The Celebrity Traitors , and 2021 London Mayoral independent candidate. Doing a Batman bit would fit Omilana's public profile, especially since he also did something similar a while back, when he set up a fake pop-up store and gave away free mobile phones to protest the rising costs of technology.
Photo: Instagram/London's Batman Omilana, on his part, seemingly has tried to disassociate from Batman , recently posting a video of himself in New York, as if to say he wasn't even in London when these things were happening. The Internet being the Internet, this is actually seen as "proof" that he is the Batman.
Speculation aside, London's Batman is the hero we need, if only to regain hope. To paraphrase one commenter, he might not be able to move properly or fight, but he'll "just pay for everything. Now that's a real hero." Hard agree. This 1958 Chevy Impala Sells With Both a 283 and a 348 Tri-Power, Full Restoration Needed
32 photos
Photo: eBay seller happyhomerenovations4u-4
Say what you want about this 1958 Chevy Impala , but once you discover the full package, there’s a good chance you’ll want to get your hands on it. This car is a project, but the owner isn’t just selling an Impala. He’s selling a full project whose next destination under the hood is in the hands of the buyer.
This is because the sale includes not one but two engines. You get both a 283 and a 348 Tri-Power, and while the choice might seem obvious, it all comes down to your plans for this car.
A 1958 Impala with a 348 under the hood can easily become a head-turning machine for a very simple reason: this was the top full-size configuration you could get in the late ‘50s.
Photo: eBay seller happyhomerenovations4u-4 Chevrolet needed just two years to decide that the Impala deserved to advance from the drawing board to the assembly lines. The carmaker attended GM’s motor show in 1956 with an Impala concept, and once the Tri-Five magic came to an end in 1957, it was time for the Impala to go past the drawing board.
The 1958 release took place as part of the Bel Air family. As the top Bel Air configuration, the Impala saw daylight in two body styles, namely convertible and hardtop. The convertible has become particularly desirable today, but coupes are also sought-after with the right engine under the hood.
And this right engine is none other than the 348. The new big-block option debuted alongside the Impala in multiple variations, and the top used three carburetors. The Tri-Power setup turned the Impala into a collectible many wealthy people would pay high dollars for, especially if the rest of the boxes are checked.
Eventually, the Impala became Chevrolet’s money-making machine, propelling the parent company to the leading spot in the United States. It also became America’s best-selling car and secured the leading spot for many years. It gained series status in 1959, in some ways turning the Bel Air , the model that brought home the bacon during the ‘50s, into the backup plan for people who were in the market for a full-size Chevrolet.
Photo: eBay seller happyhomerenovations4u-4 That’s why I think that this Impala comes with a very intriguing promise. The seller says the car is in builder condition, but the more appealing offering takes place in the mechanical department.
You’ll get a 283ci engine and a 348 unit with a 3-deuce intake manifold. None of the two is running, and that’s all the information we’re getting at this point. You should obviously send your mechanic to inspect the two engines, but the carburetors are missing, so it’s pretty clear that putting either of the two in this Impala will require some work.
Restoring a 1958 Impala, especially with a 348, isn’t an easy thing, so if you’re still new in this business, you’d rather ask a good mechanic to help you. Otherwise, if you just want a regular driver that can turn heads, the 283 is a solid choice.
The 283 was the base V8 engine in 1958, though Chevrolet also offered a four-barrel version as an option. The six was the right choice for people who wanted an Impala or a Bel Air for going to the supermarket or picking up the kids from school, but otherwise, the right choice for buyers interested in a boost of power was the 348.
Photo: eBay seller happyhomerenovations4u-4 Otherwise, this Impala comes in good metal shape, though my recommendation is that you still see everything in person. Look for signs of previous repairs, especially once you raise the car on a lift to check the underside.
The metal isn’t spotless, and the chrome needs additional work to shine as it did on day one, but overall, this Impala isn’t a rust bucket or anything similar. The cabin looks to be in good shape, and the good news is that it’s complete, so you won’t spend much time online looking for parts.
As for the price, nobody expects an Impala selling with a 348 to be cheap, right?
Photo: eBay seller happyhomerenovations4u-4 This solid project landed on eBay with a $30,000 price tag, but the owner also enabled the Make Offer option on the auction site, so you could save a few dollars with the right negotiation skills.
The listing is configured to expire in 21 days, so you have three full weeks to convince your significant other that you need another Impala project in your garage. The owner parked this project in their garage in Hernando, Mississippi, and you will obviously need transportation to take it home, considering no engine is currently under the hood.
A clean title is also available, but no other paperwork is included in the sale, which is quite a shame, considering that with the right restoration, this 1958 Impala can become a head-turning machine that would definitely win prizes easily.

Image: Peak Energy
GM has partnered with Peak Energy to develop next-generation sodium-ion battery cells, but they’re not going into EVs – they’re for grid-scale energy storage projects. GM Ventures is making a strategic investment in Peak Energy.
June 10, 2026: Under the partnership, GM will develop the sodium-ion cells in its Michigan battery labs and retain exclusive manufacturing rights. Peak Energy will integrate the cells into its battery storage systems as it ramps up US manufacturing.
The companies are targeting a market that’s growing rapidly as utilities add battery storage to support renewable energy, rising electricity demand, and the buildout of data centers and AI infrastructure.
Today’s stationary storage market is dominated by lithium-iron phosphate (LFP) batteries. But Peak Energy believes sodium-ion batteries can deliver a lower-cost alternative for grid applications, where energy density is less important than cost, reliability, and safety.

A key part of Peak’s pitch is its passively cooled battery storage platform. Conventional LFP battery systems require active cooling equipment to maintain safe operating temperatures, adding cost and complexity. Peak says its system eliminates those cooling systems entirely.
According to the company, its sodium-ion platform can reduce energy storage costs by 20% compared with conventional systems while delivering more than 99% uptime.
Peak also argues that its design wastes less energy. It estimates that replacing conventional LFP storage systems with its passively cooled technology could reduce annual battery-storage energy waste in the US by up to 2 terawatt-hours. That’s enough electricity to power a mid-sized city for a year.
GM’s vice president of battery and sustainability, Kurt Kelty, said sodium-ion is a strong fit for stationary storage.
“At GM, we know that the application should determine the battery, and for grid-scale stationary storage, sodium-ion is the right solution,” Kelty said. “Peak is already demonstrating the value of sodium-ion through their innovative energy storage platform, and together we’re working to push those benefits even further with our next-generation cell – helping deliver more reliable, lower-cost energy storage at scale for the US grid.”
Sodium-ion batteries still account for a small share of the global battery market, but interest is growing because they can be made from more abundant, lower-cost materials than lithium-based batteries. GM and Peak are betting those advantages could make sodium-ion an increasingly attractive option for large-scale energy storage. But don’t expect GM to develop sodium-ion battery cells for EVs, because the energy density is too low.
October 23, 2026, update: Peak Energy has raised $108 million in an oversubscribed Series B funding round led by GM Ventures, with backing from LG Technology Ventures and other investors.
